hints.title: Cycle Detection Without Extra Space
hints.text: Visiting nodes indefinitely without an end implies a loop. How can you detect this without storing visited node references in extra space?

hints.title: Relative Speed Catch-up Invariant
hints.text: If two runners traverse at different speeds (one step versus two steps per tick), the faster runner closes the gap by one node each step and must meet the slower runner inside any loop.

hints.title: Tortoise and Hare Traversal
hints.text: Initialize slow = head and fast = head. While fast and fast.next are not null, advance slow by 1 step and fast by 2 steps. If slow and fast point to the same node, return true. If fast reaches null, return false.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in list (0 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Floyd cycle finding traverses at most N + K steps where K is cycle length.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Storing visited node references in a set takes O(N) extra space. The follow-up specifically asks for O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm achieves O(N) time with O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Checking fast and fast.next for null before advancing, understanding that the relative speed is 1 node per iteration guaranteeing collision within cycle length, and O(1) space.
